boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Georgia Tech spaces for quiet focus, collaborative work, outdoor breaks, recreation, reflection, and community—each with a documented campus use.

cards.title: Take the Study Break Upstairs
cards.subtitle: An open-air roof garden above Clough Commons
cards.notes: Bring a short reading or take a between-class reset upstairs; check the Library hours page first because rooftop access ends before the building closes.
cards.short_summary: A planted rooftop for daylight study breaks and fresh air above Clough Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: The Georgia Tech Library identifies Clough Roof Garden as a space open to students, staff, and faculty and publishes current outdoor-access hours.
cards.access_notes: Open to students, staff, and faculty. The Library hours page currently lists Monday-Friday 7:30 a.m.-6 p.m. and weekends 9 a.m.-5 p.m.; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Move a Work Session Outdoors
cards.subtitle: The Library terrace overlooking campus and Midtown
cards.notes: Use the terrace for a daylight outline review or conversation, then move indoors before its posted 9 p.m. closing or if weather changes.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Library terrace that extends a campus work session into the open air.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library lists Crosland Terrace as an outdoor Library space and publishes access from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. seven days a week.
cards.access_notes: Current posted terrace hours are 7 a.m.-9 p.m. daily. Library access outside visitor hours may require current Georgia Tech affiliation.

cards.title: Spread Out on the Grove Level
cards.subtitle: Collaborative seating inside Price Gilbert Memorial Library
cards.notes: Choose the stair seating or a collaborative area when your work benefits from conversation, power, and room to arrange notes or devices together.
cards.short_summary: A flexible Library level built around reading and collaborative work areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library says the Grove Level contains a new-book reading room and collaborative spaces with power and data ports for study sessions.
cards.source_title: Collaborative & Quiet Study Spaces | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: Located in Price Gilbert Memorial Library. Visitor access is limited to posted Library visitor hours; affiliated users should follow BuzzCard access rules.

cards.title: Give the Project Room to Get Messy
cards.subtitle: A collaborative making space on Crosland Tower’s second floor
cards.notes: Bring a model, large document, or brainstorming prompt; use the rolling whiteboards and broad tables when an ordinary desk constrains the work.
cards.short_summary: A low-tech studio where teams can draw, build, rearrange, and think aloud.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library describes the second-floor studio as a collaborative space with large tables, rolling whiteboards, and stools for making, drawing, and building.
cards.source_title: Innovation & Ideation Studio | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Crosland Tower and available whenever the Library is open; Library entry restrictions still apply.

cards.title: Find the Graduate-Only Quiet Floor
cards.subtitle: BuzzCard-accessible study space on Crosland Tower’s sixth floor
cards.notes: Graduate students can bring quiet solo work here when shared floors feel too active; keep a BuzzCard ready for entry to the dedicated community space.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated graduate-student area for quiet work inside the Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Library identifies the sixth-floor Graduate Student Community as a BuzzCard-accessible space for graduate students and quiet study.
cards.source_title: Collaborative & Quiet Study Spaces | Georgia Tech Library
cards.access_notes: Restricted to Georgia Tech graduate students with BuzzCard access; available for quiet study whenever the Library is open.

cards.title: Switch from Studying to Social Time
cards.subtitle: A graduate lounge inside the John Lewis Student Center
cards.notes: Use the huddle room for a small conversation or borrow a game during staffed hours; groups larger than ten need a confirmed reservation.
cards.short_summary: A graduate-only lounge combining soft seating, games, a kitchenette, and a huddle room.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech says the lounge is for graduate students to connect and provides a huddle room, games, billiards, televisions, and a kitchenette.
cards.source_title: Graduate Student Lounge | Student and Campus Event Centers
cards.access_notes: Staffed daily 10 a.m.-9 p.m.; active Georgia Tech graduate students have 24-hour BuzzCard access. Groups larger than ten must reserve.

cards.title: Protect a Quiet Pause
cards.subtitle: A shared reflection room in the John Lewis Student Center
cards.notes: Step in for prayer, meditation, or quiet reflection; leave food outside and reserve ahead if your group will include ten or more people.
cards.short_summary: A campus room intentionally maintained for quiet spiritual and emotional wellness.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech designates the room for quiet contemplation, reflection, prayer, and meditation by students, staff, and faculty.
cards.source_title: Beth Cabrera Reflection Space | Student and Campus Event Centers
cards.access_notes: Staffed daily 10 a.m.-9 p.m.; the Georgia Tech community may enter with a BuzzCard when unstaffed or locked. Groups of ten or more require reservations.

cards.title: Meet Around a Real Table
cards.subtitle: An open community lounge on the Student Center’s third floor
cards.notes: Bring a study group or commuter lunch and use the tables and kitchenette; return moved furniture to its original arrangement before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A relaxed, configurable lounge supporting study, campus programs, and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech describes the lounge as open and reservable for the campus community, with study and event seating, a kitchenette, and audiovisual equipment.
cards.source_title: Southern Company Multicultural Lounge | Student and Campus Event Centers
cards.access_notes: Staffed daily 10 a.m.-9 p.m. Events require advance reservation under special-use-space rules; general users must observe posted availability.

cards.title: Trade Screens for a Shared Game
cards.subtitle: Bowling and billiards on the Student Center’s first floor
cards.notes: Stop by for bowling or billiards and ask the desk about current availability and charges before committing; event use requires advance booking.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation room with six bowling lanes, billiards, and shared seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech identifies Tech Rec as a first-floor Student Center recreation space for students and the campus community, with six bowling lanes and billiards tables.
cards.source_title: Reservable Spaces | Student and Campus Event Centers
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the John Lewis Student Center. Hours, lane availability, equipment access, and charges vary; confirm with Tech Rec staff.

cards.title: Join the Campus Growing Space
cards.subtitle: A living classroom near Paper & Clay and the Instructional Center
cards.notes: Visit the garden to observe what is growing, or contact Students Organizing for Sustainability before volunteering or working in a planting area.
cards.short_summary: A shared campus garden for volunteering, food growing, and hands-on sustainability learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia Tech Campus Services says the Community Garden is open to students, faculty, staff, and visitors for volunteering, food growing, and sustainable-gardening education.
cards.access_notes: Located near Paper & Clay and the Instructional Center. Contact Students Organizing for Sustainability for current volunteer participation details.
